extracted.intended_audience: practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO (patent/trademark attorneys), OED staff, and those involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural requirements, and sanctions governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO, especially handling of client funds, recordkeeping, timely remittance of USPTO fees, and probationary compliance following discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on commingling client funds (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(b) by commingling funds belonging to the practitioner or the practitioner's firm with advanced funds belonging to a client, and by failing to deposit unearned client funds in a sequestered account and commingling his personal and business funds with funds of his clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although 'funds advanced for costs were permitted ... to be deposited in the operating account,' the practitioner has a fiduciary responsibility for preserving those funds such that the funds could not be impermissibly invaded and depleted. Examples: depositing client payments into operating account and later issuing checks that caused depletion when presented for collection. Misconduct includes impermissibly invading advanced client funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to properly and timely remit funds to pay USPTO fees (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(4), 10.23(b)(6), 10.23(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations include failing to properly or timely remit funds received by a practitioner or the practitioner's firm from a client to pay a fee which the client is required by law to pay to the Office, and filing checks with the Office drawn on an operating bank account without maintaining sufficient funds when the checks were presented for collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely remit can result in notices of incomplete filings, loss of filing date, application abandonment, or denial of petitions. Practitioners must ensure funds intended for USPTO fees are available when checks are presented; if checks are dishonored, the practitioner must pay applicable surcharges and rectify the payment promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of entrusted legal matters (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to timely pay fees to the Office for which the client had advanced funds and otherwise neglecting entrusted legal matters (e.g., failure to timely file a Statement of Use in a Trademark application) constitutes neglect under 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect can lead to abandonment of applications and other client harm. Practitioners must track deadlines and ensure required Office actions/fees are completed on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining escrow/IOLTA accounts and segregation of unearned funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must maintain funds received from clients in IOLTA (sequestered) accounts where required, and must not commingle unearned client funds in operating accounts in a way that permits impermissible invasion or depletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires certification of compliance with rules regarding (a) maintaining funds received from clients in IOLTA accounts, (b) managing law practice trust and operating accounts. The respondent had not maintained an escrow account, did not regularly reconcile, and did not use client ledgers; remedial action included opening and properly using an escrow account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and accounting practices (reconciliation & ledgers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must regularly reconcile accounts, maintain running balances, and utilize client ledgers to track unearned fees and advanced costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent 'did not regularly reconcile or even maintain a running balance in his operating account, nor did he utilize any form of ledger for clients.' As part of probation, the respondent must 'prepare and submit a report ... certifying his compliance with proper recordkeeping procedures and also file escrow account reconciliations for each month ... at six months, 12 months, 18 months and 24 months after the date of the Final Order.' If not in compliance, the report must identify each disciplinary rule implicated and explain departures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining calendaring systems for timely rendering of legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners should maintain and utilize both an electronic and manual calendaring system to assist in the timely rendering of legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly requires, as part of the probation reporting, certification regarding maintaining and utilizing both electronic and manual calendaring systems. Failure to maintain such systems that result in missed deadlines can be evidence of neglect or inadequate practice management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to pay returned-check processing fees and surcharges (37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a check submitted to the USPTO is dishonored, practitioners must pay the processing fees/surcharge required by 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent 'paid to the Office, from his own funds, all outstanding fees required by 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m) for the processing of dishonored checks.' Payment of such fees is part of corrective action and may be considered in mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation is prohibited under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Stayed Suspension summarizes violations including 10.23(b)(4) for conduct involving dishonesty; commingling and failing to preserve client funds can overlap with dishonest or deceitful conduct depending on facts. Admissions and remedial efforts may mitigate but do not eliminate the prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions structure: stay of suspension and probation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose a suspension (here, two years) but stay execution conditioned on a probationary period with specific terms; if probation conditions are satisfied, the suspension need not be served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions enumerated include: (1) not committing misconduct violating USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility during probation; (2) timely, completely and successfully complying with directions of the Final Order; (3) periodic reporting and escrow reconciliations; and (4) completing specified legal ethics education. The practitioner is permitted to practice during probation unless the stay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural response and consequences for noncompliance during probation (Order to Show Cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply during probation, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the practitioner, and grant fifteen (15) days to respond; if noncompliance persists, the OED Director may request the USPTO Director to lift the stay and impose immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure details: (a) OED issues Order to Show Cause and provides address of record; (b) 15 days to respond; (c) after considering response, OED may deliver Order, response, and evidence to USPTO Director and request lifting stay to impose suspension; (d) any review by practitioner of lifting decision does not postpone suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reporting and publication of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the OED Reading Room and in the Official Gazette and give notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where practitioner is admitted, and the public, per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes a Notice of Stayed Suspension with specifics of violations and conduct. The record of the disciplinary proceeding shall be considered in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide Final Order to affected clients and file affidavit
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall provide, within 30 days of the Final Order, a copy of the Final Order to identified clients and shall file, within 45 days, an affidavit with the OED Director stating compliance with this requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines are strict: 30 days to notify clients; 45 days to file affidavit of compliance. This ensures clients are informed of discipline affecting their matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial education requirement (legal ethics course)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must enroll in and successfully complete a three-credit Legal Ethics course (LGST 204 or PLGL 204 at University of Maryland University College) and provide evidence of successful completion within one year of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of passing grade must be submitted to the OED Director. Completion of mandated coursework is a condition of probation and a means to remediate ethical deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors relevant to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating factors include payment of all fees for which checks were originally presented, payment of fees arising from untimely payments, paying returned-check processing fees from personal funds, acknowledgment of wrongfulness, undertaking remedial action (opening and properly using an escrow account), and no further dishonored checks since a specified date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes these mitigating facts (e.g., Respondent 'has paid all the fees ...', 'has acknowledged the wrongfulness', 'has opened, and is properly using, an escrow account', and 'has not submitted any checks drawn on an account having insufficient funds since September 2, 2009') and they can influence the nature and extent of sanctions (e.g., stayed suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's authority to seek further discipline (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking further discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the stay of the suspension to be lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the stay is lifted due to subsequent misconduct, the Office may pursue further proceedings and disseminate information in accordance with relevant rules (e.g., § 11.59). Prior record may be used as aggravating evidence.
